Job Description

The Simulated Patient Program Coordinator is responsible for the comprehensive management of the Simulated Patient (SP) Program and provides logistic and operational support for simulation events. This role recruits, trains, and manages individuals from the local community —who portray clinical scenarios, enabling medical students to practice essential interviewing, physical examination, and communication skills.

The coordinator serves as the primary liaison among faculty, staff, learners, and SPs to ensure simulation activities are realistic, standardized, and directly aligned with educational objectives. As the lead SP trainer, this role oversees case portrayal accuracy, inter-rater reliability, and program operations—including budget tracking, administrative documentation, and SP compensation processes—in full alignment with ASPE Standards of Best Practice (SOBP) and International Nursing Association for Clinical Simulation and Learning (INACSL) Standards of Best Practice.

Specific Responsibilities

Administration
and Operations

Oversee recruitment, selection, onboarding, and retention of a diverse SP pool to support varied curricular and assessment needs across programs.
Coordinate SP participation for training sessions, rehearsals, OSCEs, and live simulation-based educational activities.
Supports and assists the medical director in the training and evaluation of the clinical faculty engaged with the program as the administrative needs of that group of faculty.
Manage SP scheduling, attendance tracking, and payroll/compensation documentation in collaboration with the Director of Simulation.
Maintain SP software systems, tracking performance data, evaluations, and program metrics to support continuous quality improvement.
Participate in and lead quality improvement processes.
Resolve and/or report SP or student issues to the Director of Simulation and the Associate Dean for Preclinical Professional Education and Experiences in accordance with institutional procedures.
Communicate effectively and handle challenging or confidential matters with the utmost professionalism.
Monitor and coordinate SP program budget with the Director of Simulation.
Work with the Director of Simulation to develop and update policies, procedures, and processes related to the SP program.
Support the development and delivery of OSCE events at the College of Osteopathic Medicine (COM) for establishment and evaluation of clinical and professional skills; high-stakes, multi-station OSCE or C3DO national osteopathic licensure examination events.

Teaching/Training

Design, implement, and evaluate SP training programs to ensure authentic case portrayal, standardized delivery (affect, history, physical cues), and consistent learner assessment.
Serve as lead trainer for inter-rater reliability during high-stakes evaluations; coach or remediate SPs who deviate from scoring protocols or portrayal standards.
Assist in monitoring SP performance. This includes all aspects of case portrayal, such as delivery details, affect, and physical simulation. This may involve observing videos of SPs for quality assurance purposes to ensure standardization and implement retraining.
Ensure best practices are being implemented on-site in coordination with the ASPE and INACSL standards.

Research and Scholarly Activity

Participate as necessary in research activities in the Simulation Center.
Support outcome research and evaluation of the delivery of OSCE events at the COM for establishment and evaluation of clinical and professional skills among students.

Service

Foster a positive, respectful and confidential culture and environment amongst the students, faculty, and KHSU
Perform other duties assigned by the Director of Simulation

Supervises the simulated patient participants.

As a Personal Injury Case Manager, you'll be the steady, reassuring point of contact who guides injured clients through what is often a stressful and unfamiliar process while keeping their cases organized and moving. Exceptional client support is at the heart of this role: you'll check in on clients' recovery, keep them informed, and make sure they feel genuinely cared for from intake through settlement. Alongside that, you'll track high stakes deadlines, coordinate medical treatment and records, manage insurance, repairs, and keep attorneys aligned. If you love helping people, bringing order to complexity, and being the person everyone can count on, this role is for you.

What you'll do:

Deliver Exceptional Client Support

Serve as a warm, reliable point of contact guiding clients through the process and making them feel supported at every step
Ensure client introductions are completed and maintain regular communication schedules, including check ins on treatment and recovery
Respond to client questions and concerns promptly and with empathy
Coordinate reassignment communications and handle non responsive client follow up, keeping clients engaged in both their treatment and their case
Help facilitate smooth attorney and client communication overall

Manage Treatment, Records & Insurance

Monitor each client's medical treatment-help ensure they are treating consistently, flag gaps in care, and track progress toward maximum medical improvement
Order, follow up on, and organize medical records and billing from providers
Identify and track all applicable insurance coverage (at fault/liability, UM/UIM, MedPay, and health) — including carriers, claim numbers, adjusters, and policy limits
Negotiate with medical providers to help maximize the client's net recovery
Track medical and health insurance liens (including Medicare/Medi Cal where applicable) and letters of protection, and support timely lien resolution
Coordinate vehicle repairs and property damage resolution for auto accident clients
Help assemble and coordinate demand packages, and track demand and settlement deadlines
Once a case settles, prepare the client's breakdown of costs, expenses, and liens (net to client settlement statement)

Keep Cases Moving

Attend attorney meetings and capture key decisions, action items, and deadlines
Maintain and update case blueprints and the case management tracker to reflect current case status, treatment status, and case progress
Monitor critical deadlines including but not limited to the Statute of Limitations uninsured/underinsured motorist (UM/UIM) demand deadlines, and demand/settlement deadlines; for cases that proceed to litigation, track applicable court deadlines
Keep cases advancing from intake through treatment, demand, and settlement — following up so nothing stalls
Track case progress and report updates during monthly team meetings

Coordinate Scheduling & Coverage

Schedule and coordinate depositions, medical examinations (IME/DME), mediations, and hearings
Resolve scheduling conflicts in coordination with attorneys
Monitor team communications to ensure scheduling needs are addressed quickly

Requirements

At least one year of experience in personal injury case management is required
Must be fluent in Spanish
A genuine customer service mindset — you're empathetic and patient, and you take pride in making clients feel cared for
Strong organizational and time management skills — you can juggle multiple priorities without dropping the ball
Clear, confident written and verbal communication
A proactive mindset: you spot problems before they become emergencies
A collaborative team player who works well across departments — including comfort coordinating with medical providers and insurance adjusters
Comfort reading and organizing medical records and bills is a plus
Must be flexible and comfortable working extended hours as needed to support litigation deadlines, trial schedules, and case demands
This is a full time, on site role. Standard hours are Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with overtime required when necessary to meet litigation deadlines, trial schedules, and case demands

Industry-Leading Benefits:

Firm pays 100% of premiums for dental and vision
Firm pays 100% of all Silver-level medical plans
Firm contributes approximately 10% toward retirement (3% Safe Harbor + 7% Profit Sharing)
$500 annual FSA contribution

At Dungarvin, we are dedicated to making a meaningful impact in the lives of individuals with diverse abilities. We provide essential support to those with intellectual and developmental disabilities, physical disabilities, autism, and mental health conditions - empowering them to thrive in their communities. Where barriers exist, we create pathways for inclusion and independence.

About our Adult Day Program:

Our Adult Day Program provides structured daytime services for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Individuals participate in skill-building, recreational, educational, and community-based activities that support independence, social connection, and personal goals. Staff work directly with individuals throughout the day, providing instruction, encouragement, personal care, behavioral support, and opportunities for meaningful participation.

The Role:

We are looking for an organized, confident, and proactive Program Coordinator for our Adult Day Program in Long Beach, CA.

The Program Coordinator (PC) is the lead Direct Support Professional (DSP) within the program. This is a hands-on working lead role, not a traditional administrative or supervisory position.

The PC works directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities throughout the day, providing personal care, instruction, skill development, and positive behavioral support. The goal is simple: keep individuals safe, engaged, supported, and moving toward greater independence.

The PC also helps keep the program running. This includes coordinating daily activities, adjusting schedules, supporting documentation, reinforcing expectations, and providing day-to-day guidance to DSP staff. The PC reports to the Program Director and leads through communication, consistency, and example, without formal supervisory authority.

Why You’ll Love This Role:

Competitive Pay:
$23.75/hour
Full Range Scale
: $23.75 - $26.45 per hour ( The starting rate for this position is fixed at $23.75 per hour. Pay increases occur over time and are tied to tenure/length of employment with Dungarvin.)
Meaningful Work:
Help individuals build skills, independence, and community connections
Leadership Opportunities:
Lead by example while coaching, guiding, and supporting staff
Variety:
Balance direct support, daily scheduling, staff guidance, communication, and program coordination.
Community Connections:
Help build partnerships and foster a vibrant, inclusive program environment.
Professional Growth:
Develop leadership, communication, documentation, and program coordination skills while continuing to work directly with the people we support.

Full Time Monday-Friday, daytime hours

Growth and Development Opportunities
Employee Referral Program
Employee Assistance Program
National Brand Discounts
TapCheck – access up to 50% of your pay before payday

training and orientation

The Program Coordinator provides direct support to individuals while helping coordinate the daily flow of the Adult Day Program and ensuring staff are supported and aligned.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Provide hands-on direct support to adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
Assist individuals with personal care, hygiene, mobility, meals, communication, community participation, and other daily needs.
Model and implement behavior supports, including de-escalation techniques during challenging situations
Support individuals in achieving personal goals and increasing independence
Lead by example and provide day-to-day guidance, coaching, and support to DSP staff
Complete accurate and timely progress notes, reports, data tracking, and other required documentation
Assist with individual goals, ISP updates, and documentation expectations
Assist with basic program operations; coordinate transportation, community activities, program supplies, and other daily operational needs
Communicate professionally and effectively with families, providers, and interdisciplinary teams
Follow established health, safety, licensing, medication, transportation, and program procedures
Communicate concerns, changes, or operational challenges to the Program Director
Maintain the rights, dignity, health, safety, and confidentiality of the individuals served

Qualifications

Education & Experience:

Bachelors degree in Human Services, Special Education, or related field is preferred . Or, equivalent training/experience in disability services will be considered.
A minimum of one (1) year of experience supporting individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities is required.

At least one (1) year of experience in adult day program, vocational program, residential program, behavioral health setting, educational setting, or other community-based disability service

Confident and professional communicator

Strong written communication and documentation skills
Organized and able to manage multiple responsibilities throughout the day

Calm, adaptable, creative, and solution-focused

Comfortable working directly with individuals who may require personal care, behavioral support, mobility assistance, or physical assistance
Able to maintain professional relationships with individuals, staff, families, residential providers, Regional Center representatives, and other community partners
Tech savvy with computers, electronic documentation systems, email, spreadsheets, and other workplace technology

As a Personal Injury Case Manager, you'll be the steady, reassuring point of contact who guides injured clients through what is often a stressful and unfamiliar process while keeping their cases organized and moving. Exceptional client support is at the heart of this role: you'll check in on clients' recovery, keep them informed, and make sure they feel genuinely cared for from intake through settlement. Alongside that, you'll track high stakes deadlines, coordinate medical treatment and records, manage insurance, repairs, and keep attorneys aligned. If you love helping people, bringing order to complexity, and being the person everyone can count on, this role is for you.

What you'll do:

Deliver Exceptional Client Support

Serve as a warm, reliable point of contact guiding clients through the process and making them feel supported at every step
Ensure client introductions are completed and maintain regular communication schedules, including check ins on treatment and recovery
Respond to client questions and concerns promptly and with empathy
Coordinate reassignment communications and handle non responsive client follow up, keeping clients engaged in both their treatment and their case
Help facilitate smooth attorney and client communication overall

Manage Treatment, Records & Insurance

Monitor each client's medical treatment-help ensure they are treating consistently, flag gaps in care, and track progress toward maximum medical improvement
Order, follow up on, and organize medical records and billing from providers
Identify and track all applicable insurance coverage (at fault/liability, UM/UIM, MedPay, and health) — including carriers, claim numbers, adjusters, and policy limits
Negotiate with medical providers to help maximize the client's net recovery
Track medical and health insurance liens (including Medicare/Medi Cal where applicable) and letters of protection, and support timely lien resolution
Coordinate vehicle repairs and property damage resolution for auto accident clients
Help assemble and coordinate demand packages, and track demand and settlement deadlines
Once a case settles, prepare the client's breakdown of costs, expenses, and liens (net to client settlement statement)

Keep Cases Moving

Attend attorney meetings and capture key decisions, action items, and deadlines
Maintain and update case blueprints and the case management tracker to reflect current case status, treatment status, and case progress
Monitor critical deadlines including but not limited to the Statute of Limitations uninsured/underinsured motorist (UM/UIM) demand deadlines, and demand/settlement deadlines; for cases that proceed to litigation, track applicable court deadlines
Keep cases advancing from intake through treatment, demand, and settlement — following up so nothing stalls
Track case progress and report updates during monthly team meetings

Coordinate Scheduling & Coverage

Schedule and coordinate depositions, medical examinations (IME/DME), mediations, and hearings
Resolve scheduling conflicts in coordination with attorneys
Monitor team communications to ensure scheduling needs are addressed quickly

Requirements

At least one year of experience in personal injury case management is required
Must be fluent in Spanish
A genuine customer service mindset — you're empathetic and patient, and you take pride in making clients feel cared for
Strong organizational and time management skills — you can juggle multiple priorities without dropping the ball
Clear, confident written and verbal communication
A proactive mindset: you spot problems before they become emergencies
A collaborative team player who works well across departments — including comfort coordinating with medical providers and insurance adjusters
Comfort reading and organizing medical records and bills is a plus
Must be flexible and comfortable working extended hours as needed to support litigation deadlines, trial schedules, and case demands
This is a full time, on site role. Standard hours are Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with overtime required when necessary to meet litigation deadlines, trial schedules, and case demands

new_jobs.description:
Become a part of our caring community

The Medical Social Worker, reporting to the Clinical Manager, participates in the interdisciplinary care provided to home health patients. You will function to evaluate and develop a plan of care personalized to fit the patient's emotional and social needs. The Medical Social Worker will provide direction and supervision of the Social Worker Assistant when involved in the patient's plan of care. The Medical Social Worker works within CenterWell Home Health's company-specific policy and procedures, applicable healthcare standards, governmental laws, and regulations.

As The Medical Social Worker, You Will

Assess the patient's social and emotional state as it relates to their illness or injury, needs for care and their response to such treatment, and adjustments to care.
Assess any relationships of the patient's medical and nursing needs in the home setting, financial resources, and available community resources.
Provide any appropriate action to obtain available community resources to help resolve issues that may impede the patient's recovery.
Communicate with patients and their family members, and associates in the organization.
Provide ongoing assessment of patient and family needs and responses to understanding the treatment process and coping with social and emotional responses
Participate as a member of the interdisciplinary care team in care coordination activities and act as a resource to other health team members in the identification and resolution of patient needs
Evaluate the performance of the Social Work Assistant (BSW) to assure that all medical social services are provided to patients in compliance with Company, government, and professional standards
Maintain and submit documentation as required by the company and/ or facility including any case conferences, patient/physician community contacts, visit reports progress notes, and confers with other health care disciplines in providing optimum patient care.

Required Qualifications

Use your skills to make an impact

Minimum of one year of experience as a social worker in a health care setting, home health, and/or hospice.
Social Worker licensure in the state of practice, if required by state law or regulation.
A valid driver's license, auto insurance, and reliable transportation.
Proof of current CPR certification
Experience with discharge planning needs, and obtaining community resources (housing, shelter, funeral/memorial service arrangements, legal, information and referral, state/federal financial and medication programs, and eligibility).
Knowledge of medications and their correct administration.
Demonstrated ability to organize tasks, develop action plans, set priorities, and function under stressful situations.
Flexibility in work hours and travel locally.
Maintain current licensure certifications and meet mandatory continuing education requirements.
Must read, write and speak fluent English.
